newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech min sees Budvar privatisation plan in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Czech min sees Budvar privatisation plan in Feb.

text.p: The Czech agriculture ministry should present a plan in February for the privatisation of brewery Budvar n.p., maker of the disputed Budweiser brand beer, the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes reported on Friday.
The paper quoted Jiri Stehlik, head of the ministry's privatisation department, as saying that if all goes according to plan, the plan may be decided upon by the end of the year.
"We should submit a proposal to the government in February, and it is realistic that the privatisation could be decided this year," Stehlik said.
Neither ministry nor brewery officials were immediately available for comment.
The ministry was to submit a plan to privatise the brewery before the end of 1996, after trademark talks with Anheuser- Busch Cos collapsed near the end of September.
The talks over the use of the "Budweiser" and "Bud" trademarks were aimed at resolving a long-standing disagreement which prohibits the rivals from selling their labels in the other's key markets.

Anheuser-Busch sells its beer under the Budweiser name in 11 European countries and under the "Bud" name in nine other European countries. Both brands have virtually identical labels except for the name.
Agriculture Minister Josef Lux has said there is little chance that A-B would take part in the Ceske Budejovice (Budweis) brewery, seen by many Czechs as a piece of national heritage.
The Czech government has been mulling the privatisation of Budvar with and without participation of A-B, but had held off taking any steps before the end of the trademark talks.
